metadata.title: PIAAC PROBLEM SOLVING IN TECHNOLOGY-RICH ENVIRONMENTS: A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a conceptual framework for the PIAAC PS-TRE domain and does not report an analyzed student micro-dataset, sampling frame, or weighting variables. It specifies how the domain will be assessed (task contexts, cognitive/technology/task dimensions, and development targets for scenarios), but it does not provide a field-test or main-assessment analytic sample. As a result, no complex survey design weights (e.g., student/sampling weights or replicate weights) are described or applied here. For any later empirical implementation of PS-TRE in PIAAC, analysts should use the official PIAAC sampling weights and replicate weights provided with the microdata to account for stratification and clustering; this paper itself contains no such weighting guidance.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a framework/methodology paper that defines the PS-TRE construct and outlines task and scoring development goals; it does not analyze student-level cognitive achievement outcomes with plausible values. Because no PV-based dependent variable is estimated and no empirical model is fit, plausible values handling is not applicable. Missing-data handling is also not reported because there is no dataset construction, field-test dataset, or statistical estimation procedure presented in the document.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No analytic sample is defined because the paper is a conceptual framework for the future PIAAC PS-TRE assessment. It discusses task development targets (e.g., 25 task proposals for consideration, field test scenarios, and main assessment scenarios) and recommended distributions across contexts and cognitive dimensions, but it does not specify inclusion/exclusion criteria for an empirical student dataset.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD working paper provides a conceptual framework for assessing problem solving in technology-rich environments (PS-TRE) within the OECD Programme for the International Assessment of Adult Competencies (PIAAC). It defines PS-TRE as using digital technology, communication tools and networks to acquire and evaluate information, communicate with others, and perform practical tasks, emphasizing goal setting, planning, monitoring, and information evaluation/integration. The framework organizes the domain into cognitive dimensions, technology dimensions, and task dimensions, and specifies how task characteristics (e.g., intrinsic complexity, explicitness, likelihood of impasses, and transformation/generation demands) should be represented in assessment tasks. It also outlines operational aspects such as prerequisite ICT skills, task development targets (scenario durations of 5/10/15 minutes), and the intention to capture process indicators (e.g., time, actions, and action sequences) to support scoring models. No empirical results, model performance metrics, or country-level benchmarks are reported because the paper is not an analysis of PS-TRE microdata.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction contains no empirical ML analysis because the document is a conceptual framework and assessment-design specification rather than a study that fits predictive models to PIAAC microdata. Consequently, there is no reported student sample, no PV/scaling estimation procedure, no missing-data strategy, and no performance metrics to populate main findings. The sparse fields are therefore due to the paper’s purpose (construct definition and operationalization) rather than an omission of results from an empirical study.
